Appkin runs apps described in JSON files that you make, open or are sent. Appkin has no gallery of apps: apps travel only as files, between people who choose to share them.

You are responsible for the apps you run and share and for what they load and show. Use only text, pictures and data you have the right to use, and follow the terms of the services an app connects to, such as an API's.

Apps made with an AI app can contain mistakes: check what they show before relying on it.

The examples use public-domain works from Wikimedia Commons, and data and images from TMDB under its terms; Appkin is not endorsed by TMDB.

Appkin is free, has no ads and collects no data. It is open source under the MIT licence and provided as it is, without warranty.

To report an app, its content or a problem, write to info@wakirox.app.
Masterpieces shows public-domain works; the images come from Wikimedia Commons.
The Movies example uses TMDB and the TMDB APIs but is not endorsed, certified, or otherwise approved by TMDB.
Change an example with Edit this app in its ⋮ menu, and your version is kept under Your apps.
A JSON file is plain text that describes an app: its screens, the words and pictures on them, lists, forms and buttons, and what happens when you tap something.
Open a file and Appkin draws its screens at once, with its own built-in parts: nothing in the file runs as code. Nothing to install, build or sign up for.
Try an example below, open a file someone sent you, write one in the built-in editor, or ask the AI app you already use (ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude…) to make one for you.
Every app you open is kept under Your apps. Put any of them on your phone\'s home screen with its own icon: tapping it opens that app directly.
Write one yourself: read the JSON format guide
